title: Cordon-and-drain stream protocol: client lease renewal and batch-aware GC for long-running tool-call streams
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a 'cordon-and-drain' protocol for the serving fleet to support graceful evacuation of GPU workers handling long-running streaming generations (especially function/tool-invocation workflows). The protocol provides: 1) a server-initiated cordon signal to mark a worker draining, 2) a client-visible lease-renewal handshake for in-flight generations, 3) checkpointed partial outputs and KV-cache snapshot refs to allow resume on compatible workers, and 4) batch-aware garbage collection windows to avoid premature KV eviction that would prevent client resume. Aim: zero customer-visible failure during planned worker maintenance and reduced partial-generation loss on transient disconnects.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Server can cordon workers and surface a 'draining' flag within worker metadata and in the routing layer
2) Active streaming sessions receive a lease token with expiry; SDKs attempt background lease renewal when available
3) If client disconnects but lease is valid, partial outputs remain resumable on a compatible worker for the GC grace window
4) If cordon completes and lease not renewed, partial outputs are compacted to tombstones and clients receive a resumable error with resume token
5) End-to-end test coverage simulating worker drain, client reconnect, and resumed generation across multiple workers
6) Benchmarked latency/regression report showing <2% p99 latency impact for non-draining traffic
implementation_notes: High-level steps: 1) add 'draining' flag to worker registry; 2) extend streaming protocol to include lease tokens and TTL; 3) implement KV-cache snapshot reference model; 4) routing layer honors resume token compatibility when relocating sessions; 5) add GC policy hooks that account for active lease windows and batch affinity
Lease token specifics: 64-bit monotonic id + expiry timestamp; renewals are idempotent RPCs; server maintains per-session lease metadata with last_renewal_at
KV-cache snapshot: store small manifest pointer to underlying compacted entry instead of full cache data to reduce memory duplication during worker migration
Batch-aware GC: GC should consider recent batch affinity (workers that served prefixes) and extend grace window if any client holds a valid lease to avoid KV evictions that break resume

Fallback behavior: if resume not possible, emit structured partial-output message with tombstone reason, last_valid_token, and suggestions (resend prompt or rebuild prefix) to help client SDKs recover
Backward compatibility: provide a toggle in account config to opt into lease protocol; default enabled for runtime-1.40 customers
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease issuance, renewal, expiry and idempotency
Integration test harness that simulates controlled cordon (SIGTERM with drain) and verifies client resume across two worker groups
Chaos test: random network partitions and client disconnects during long tool invocations to verify tombstone semantics
Load test demonstrating batch-aware GC does not significantly increase memory pressure: target <5% uplift in steady-state memory
SDK integration: update JS and Python SDKs to auto-renew leases when possible and include resume helpers in reconnect paths
